transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. I guess what finally made me call the employee assistance program is that I’m just barely sleeping right lately. 

I'll go to bed and just lie there replaying work stuff, or arguments from home. And then I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning. By the time I actually have to get up and start the day, I just feel like I never really rested at all.
How long has this sleep problem been going on?
I'd say it's been going on for about a year and two months now. It pretty much started right around the time the arguments at home started getting a lot worse.
When things are relatively calm at home and work, do you still have the same difficulty sleeping?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. It feels like there haven't been many calm stretches lately between the job and everything at home. So I haven't really noticed if my sleep gets better during the quiet moments... it just kind of feels like a constant issue right now.
During the daytime, do you also feel excessively worried or on edge, apart from when you are trying to sleep?

Not really, no. I mean, work has its normal pressures, but I wouldn't say I feel on edge or excessively worried during the day. Honestly, during the daytime I'm mostly just... tired from not sleeping. I kind of just put my head down and get through my work. It's really only when I lay down at night that my brain decides to start racing.
When you spend several nights away from home and work, such as on vacation, does your sleep improve?

I haven't really taken a vacation in a while, so I can't say for sure. The last time I was away for a few days was a work trip, and I didn't sleep well then either, but I was still dealing with work stuff. So, I don't really know if being completely away from it all would help.
As bedtime approaches, do you find yourself becoming preoccupied or anxious about whether you’ll be able to sleep?

Not really, no. I don't really get anxious about the sleep itself. I just... get in bed, hoping I'll drift off, but then my mind just starts going over all the stuff from the day or what I have to do tomorrow. It's not a worry about *not* sleeping, it's just that my brain won't shut off to let me sleep.
Do you ever sleep noticeably better somewhere other than your usual bed, such as on a couch or in a guest room?

No, not really. I mean, I've fallen asleep on the couch watching TV a couple of times, but I always wake up after an hour or so and move to my bed. I wouldn't say I sleep any better out there. It's pretty much the same wherever I try to sleep in the house.
When you get into bed at night, do you become noticeably alert or tense because your bed has come to feel associated with being awake?

No, I wouldn't say I feel tense or anything just from getting into bed. It's not like the bed itself makes me feel more awake. It's just... once I'm there and it's quiet, that's when my mind starts racing. But it's not the bed causing it, if that makes sense.
In a typical week, how many nights do you have trouble falling asleep or wake up and cannot get back to sleep?

It's pretty much every night. Honestly, that's what finally made me call the employee assistance program at work. I'm just barely sleeping right. I lie there replaying work stuff, or... or arguments at home, and then I usually wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and can't get back to sleep. I just start the day feeling like I never really rested at all.
Do you ever feel drowsy before getting into bed but become more alert once you lie down to sleep?

No, I don't think so. I'm usually pretty exhausted before I go to bed, but it's not like I suddenly feel wide awake as soon as I lie down. I stay physically tired, it's just... like I said, my brain won't shut off. But I definitely don't get a burst of alertness or anything.
Have there been any genuinely calm periods lasting several days when your sleep was still just as poor?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really had any calm periods lately, to be honest. It's just been a constant stress with work and things at home, so... there hasn't been a time where I felt relaxed for a few days but still couldn't sleep. The poor sleep is pretty much tied to how stressed I am.
